events.subtitle: Kawasaki Jazz 2026 — Piano Solo & Trio

venue.name: カルッツかわさき ホール

events.factual_description: Kawasaki Jazz and Culttz Kawasaki present Ai Furusato — Piano Solo & Trio on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 at Culttz Kawasaki Hall, with doors at 3:00 PM and the performance starting at 4:00 PM. The presenters describe the concert as a Kawasaki homecoming for Furusato and specify a piano-solo first set followed by a trio second set, with vocalist akiko appearing as a special guest. The announced personnel are Ai Furusato on piano and keyboard, Shunsuke Uehara on drums, Shin Sakaino on bass and akiko on vocals. Culttz Kawasaki lists reserved-seat prices of ¥4,800 general, ¥4,000 for members and ¥3,000 U18. The venue and Kawasaki Jazz identify Furusato as a 15-year-old jazz pianist who began studying piano in Kawasaki and entered Berklee College of Music's regular program at age 12 on a Presidential Scholarship. Her four-track Rise EP was released May 26, 2026 and is available on Apple Music.

en.why_it_matters: The useful thing about this homecoming is the format: Furusato opens alone, then has to solve the music again inside a trio before vocalist akiko enters the picture. For a pianist whose career has accelerated unusually early, hearing those changes of scale in one afternoon is a better reason to pay attention than the prodigy story by itself.
en.trip_verdict: If November 3 is open while you are in Greater Tokyo/Kanto, this is a smart Kawasaki afternoon to catch. I would not reshape a Tokyo stay around it, but I would take the short regional detour if the schedule lines up.

es.why_it_matters: Lo interesante de este regreso a casa está en el formato: Furusato empieza sola, después tiene que resolver la música de nuevo dentro de un trío y finalmente aparece la voz de akiko. Para una pianista cuya carrera se aceleró tan temprano, escuchar esos cambios de escala en una sola tarde dice mucho más que quedarse con la historia de la niña prodigio.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 3 de noviembre está libre mientras estás en Tokio/Kanto, sí me daría una vuelta a Kawasaki. No reorganizaría una estancia en Tokio alrededor de esta fecha, pero el desvío regional vale la pena si cuadra con el itinerario.
